value.body: A practising artist makes and sells their own work — painting, sculpture, printmaking, photography, installation or ceramics — through exhibitions, galleries, commissions and online sales. Most combine studio practice with other income such as teaching, workshops or design work, especially early on.

items.label: Ministry of Culture scholarship
items.note: Ages 18–25; up to 400 a year across art forms
items.source: CCRT Scholarships to Young Artistes scheme

items.label: National platform
items.value: Lalit Kala Akademi National Exhibition of Art
items.note: Juried; selected works are shown and some receive awards

value.title: How you get in
value.body: There is no licence or exam. A BFA/MFA gives training and a network, but artists build careers through a body of work: applying to group shows, juried exhibitions, residencies and grants, and approaching galleries and buyers.

value.title: At a glance
items: Income is irregular and uncertain, especially in the first years.
Residencies, grants and group shows are the usual first steps to visibility.
Many artists teach, take commissions or do design work to support their practice.
